notes: THE WARNINGS NOW TELL THE TRUTH, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. A warning that fires when nothing is wrong is not a cosmetic fault: you clear it, it comes back, and in time you stop reading the panel — which is where the warnings that matter are also written. This release is a deliberate sweep for that, prompted by finding one on our own machine. A BACKUP FOLDER IN ONEDRIVE IS NOW RECOGNISED AS ONE. On current macOS the folder is named for your account — OneDrive-Personal, or OneDrive followed by your organisation — and the app could not tell it was a cloud folder at all. Two consequences followed from that single miss, and the second is the serious one: it told you your backups were "on this same computer" when they were syncing perfectly well, and it said NOTHING about the fact that your entire ledger, payroll included, was sitting readable in that cloud account with no passphrase. That warning now appears when it should, and Google Drive on Windows — which mounts as its own drive letter rather than a folder — is recognised as well. ON WINDOWS, THE DISK-ENCRYPTION WARNING HAD NEVER APPEARED AT ALL. The check asked Windows about BitLocker and misread every answer it could receive, concluding "cannot tell" every time. We state plainly that the real security boundary is your computer's login and its disk encryption, because the app password does not protect the files themselves — which makes that the one warning that most needed to work. It works now. AN UNREADABLE SETTINGS FILE IS NO LONGER REPORTED AS "BACKUPS ARE OFF". The remedy that came with it — set them up again — would have overwritten a stored passphrase that may still have been recoverable, and it was being offered to people whose backups were running. The app now says the settings could not be read, and prescribes nothing until you have seen why. THE TWO-COMPUTER WARNING now recognises a machine by its name. It previously relied on a marker that travels with the files whenever a whole user profile is copied — precisely the case the warning exists for. And restoring a backup no longer causes the app to claim that no backup has been proven restorable. EVERY ACCOUNT FIELD NOW CARRIES ITS NAME. Every account, vendor, bank, unit and project picker sits beneath a heading you can read on screen; screen-reader software could not see those headings, and announced 123 of these fields as nothing at all. Each now takes its name from the heading itself, so the spoken name and the visible one cannot drift apart as the product grows. NO DATABASE CHANGE: your data and settings are untouched and this installs straight over the previous version. Please still take a backup first — Backup & Export, Back up now.
